Yes. Hansen/UMD (GFC-2025-v1.13) mapped about 81.3 ha of tree-cover loss inside the property in 2021, roughly 2.23% of its 3,643.5 ha. The method corroborated this: later years were observed, and the JRC 2020 forest reference agrees over 98% of the event area.

Context: according to the MGAP 2021 map, about 68.1 ha of the loss area is planted forest (Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda), 13.2 ha is outside mapped forest, and none is native forest. Separately, Hansen shows 37.3 ha of loss in patches under 0.5 ha, which is not counted in the 81.3 ha.

Limits: this does not show deforestation or land-use change, since Hansen loss includes plantation cutting. It also says nothing about cause, legality, responsible actor, or regulatory compliance.
